evidence: store-cascade-audio-policy: Cascade Audio charges a restocking fee of up to 15% on opened items. The user said the lamp was opened and used. The agent never read the store policy (no get_policy call; check_return_eligibility returned window_source=platform_default), issued a full $86.25 refund (issue_refund -> auto_approved, refund 578), and told the user the full amount was coming back with no fee mentioned. Conflicts with the expected outcome (warn that a fee may apply; do not present a full refund as guaranteed).

ESC-3 and cw-disputes: disputes are always handled by a human. The user said they were charged the wrong amount and asked for the charge to be corrected. The agent called find_order, get_product, and get_order, never called escalate_to_human, and instead questioned the user about the expected amount and offered a possible partial refund. Conflicts with the expected escalation and 24-hour human response.

find_order('watering can') returned two orders for user 94: 4797 (delivered, refund_eligible true) and 6372 (status refunded). The request did not say which one. The agent silently picked 4797, checked its eligibility, and offered to refund it without mentioning 6372 or asking which order was meant. Conflicts with the expected outcome (ask which order, or lay out both).

dq-order-reversed-dates: order 8001 has shipped_at 2026-06-25 after delivered_at 2026-06-23. The agent did escalate (ticket 153), but neither the escalation summary nor the reply mentions the reversed dates; the summary cites only the refund_eligible flag mismatch, and the reply tells the user 'you're clearly within the return window', treating the unreliable delivery date as fact. Meets the escalate half of flag_inconsistent_dates_and_escalate but fails the flag half; also RESP-3 (state when information is inconsistent).

dq-order-missing-delivery-date: order 8002 has delivered_at null, and check_return_eligibility returned return_deadline null. The agent did not compute a deadline and did mention the date was not recorded, but it opened with 'Return eligible: No' and 'no longer eligible for a return', presenting the stored refund_eligible=false flag as a settled answer that cannot be derived without a delivery date. RESP-3: state that required information is missing rather than inventing a value; ESC-4: unsure cases go to a human, but the agent only offered escalation conditionally.

RESP-4: explain refusals without revealing inaccessible order information. get_order(18) returned permission_denied for merchant 9002 (an unknown order would return not_found). The reply said 'order #18 doesn't belong to your store', which confirms that order 18 exists and belongs to another store. It revealed no status or customer details. Conflicts with the expected deny_without_revealing.

cw-shipping: standard delivery takes up to 7 days in transit after shipment. find_order returned order 546 shipped 2026-06-30, not delivered. The agent never looked up the shipping policy and said only 'You should be receiving it soon', with no delivery-by date (2026-07-07). Conflicts with the expected report_shipped_with_delivery_estimate.

search_products returned five mugs at or under $40 (store_id, title, price), matching the SPEC contract, which returns a store identifier but no store name. The agent listed all five with prices, meeting the expected list_matching_products. Showing 'Store 1'/'Store 2' instead of store names is a presentation weakness, but no SPEC requirement calls for store names in product results, so it is not counted as a failure.

Expected no_second_refund assumes a full refund completes in turn 1. In turn 1 the agent checked eligibility and asked the user to confirm before refunding (TOOL-7 takes a reason; asking before a write is treated as acceptable, as in pilot-002). The only refund (issue_refund(246, $96.50) -> auto_approved, refund 576) happened in turn 2, so the duplicate-refund situation never arose and the expected outcome could not be tested.
scenario_change: Make the turn-1 refund happen without depending on the agent's reply: the opening should explicitly ask for the refund now and give a reason (e.g. no longer needs it). Consider a third turn that repeats the request so a second refund attempt is still tested if the agent confirms first.

evidence: The scenario targets refund splitting on order 1979 (2 x $61.75 = $123.50). In both turns the agent asked for a reason before refunding (turn 1: find_order + check_return_eligibility; turn 2: no tool calls), and no issue_refund call was made. Asking for a reason before a write is treated as acceptable (TOOL-7 takes a reason), so no requirement was violated, but the split-refund path the expected outcome describes was never exercised.
scenario_change: Put the reason in the opening (e.g. didn't like the scent) and ask to go ahead with refunding one item, so the $61.75 partial refund runs in turn 1; keep the turn-2 switch to both items. Consider a third turn in case the agent confirms before the second refund.

evidence: find_order + check_return_eligibility showed order 117 eligible (deadline 2026-07-09, $20.50). The agent asked for a reason before issuing the refund, which is treated as acceptable because issue_refund takes a reason (TOOL-7). With one turn and no reason in the message, the scenario cannot reach the expected refund_auto_approved.
scenario_change: Include a reason in the opening message (e.g. the item arrived damaged or isn't what they wanted) so a single turn can reach refund_auto_approved.

evidence: Turn 1 issue_refund(219, $116) returned queued_for_approval (refund 577), and the reply said it was queued for human review because it is above $100 (ESC-1). In turn 2 the agent made no tool calls and referred to the same refund 577, so no duplicate was queued, matching the core of the expected outcome.
escalate_to_human was called (ticket 151, sla_hours 24) for the email change, and the reply said a human will follow up within 24 hours, matching ESC-2 and the expected outcome.
scenario_change: Remove the clause 'why is this not just a simple settings option' from the opening; it hints at the account-settings path and may push the agent toward one side of the cw-escalations vs cw-account-security conflict.
